messages.subject: some questions about graph file
parts:
I successfully converted a shape file in a graph file containing over 3000 counties in the US, but four counties shows no links (i.e., neighbors). Here is a part of the graph file:

3109
1 8 48 100 101 102 111 535 553 554
2 2 3102 3109
3 6 4 6 7 487 524 529
4 6 3 8 9 10 11 524
5 6 6 7 22 33 485 487
6 4 3 5 7 22
7 4 3 5 6 487
8 2 4 10
9 4 4 11 424 524
10 4 4 8 11 12
11 5 4 9 10 12 424
12 4 10 11 13 424
13 4 12 14 15 424
14 5 13 15 424 496 501
15 6 13 14 16 17 501 503
16 6 15 17 428 493 503 510
17 5 15 16 18 428 465
18 1 17
19 0
20 4 26 27 46 74

However, the area code (FIPS) has been entirely recoded from 1, 2, 3... so my questions are:

Q1. I'd like to see why area 19 has no adjacent county (since every county must have at least one adjacent county), but how to know the original FIPS of area 19 in this example?
Q2, Are all FIPSs sorted before recoding in the graph file?
Q3. I referred some examples in this website, and see areas in some data sets are recoded with a variable starting from 0, not 1; however, the area code in its graph file starts from 1. I guess there might be some algorithms to match the inconsistent area codes between data and graph file, but I just feel confused on how to efficiently recode my original FIPSs? If I need to recode the original FIPS variable to match the area code in the graph file, again, like Q1, how can I know which FIPS is which area code?

Any suggestion is appreciated!

Hi,

In addition to what Havard said, you may want to use a sparse Matrix as described in the FAQ:

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-I-have-a-shapefile.-How-can-I-fit-a-spatial-model-with-R-INLA-

There you will find a complete example on how to fit a spatial model, when data are from a shapefile. Before fitting the model, you can then manipulate the nb adjacency object to add neighbours or the data.frame to exclude data, etc.

HTH.

Virgilio

On Tuesday, March 17, 2015 at 5:31:15 PM UTC+1, LC Chien wrote:


On Tuesday, March 17, 2015 at 12:58:01 AM UTC-5, Havard Rue wrote:
On Mon, 2015-03-16 at 15:23 -0700, LC Chien wrote:

> Q1. I'd like to see why area 19 has no adjacent county (since every
> county must have at least one adjacent county), but how to know the
> original FIPS of area 19 in this example?

Hi,

I guess you have to plot the map and then mark region 19.

It's a good idea but I cannot directly use the graph file but the shape file to draw a map. While the shape file does not have the recoded area code inside, I still cannot identify where area 19 is from the map. If there is a way to put the recoded area code from the graph file back to the shape file, I then can identify the original FIPS code of area #19.

Hi,

I think I can answer your questions. First point to note - the poly2nb() command does not automatically give everyone a neighbour - if there are single polygons islands in your shapefile it won't assign them neighbours, which is entirely appropriate as it would be inaccurate to assign them neighbours. Of course depending on your problem and the geography you may need to later assign everyone a neighbour but then again you may not.

You can visualize the nb matrix using:

plot(nb.map, coordinates(map))

Even with 3000 rows you should be able to spot islands and that may help you figure out which counties they are when comparing to a regular map - although that is very manual. But its generally good to visualise the nb matrix anyhow as I have found it can help spot other problems.

Alternatively to visualize polygon 19 for example you can do the following to fill it blue and leave the other polygon's blank:

plot(map)
plot(map[19,], add=TRUE, col="blue")

> Q2, Are all FIPSs sorted before recoding in the graph file?

I don't know how you have created the graph file... 

Here is the program:

map <- readOGR("C:/lchien/Dropbox/diabetes/data/uscounty.shp","uscounty")
nb.map <- poly2nb(map)
nb2INLA("C:/lchien/Dropbox/asthma/data/uscounty.graph",nb.map)

I checked the manuals of readOGR(), poly2nb(), and nb2INLA() functions, but found no related option to reorder my original FIPSs. In my imagination, if the original FIPS code is reordered first, and recoded to 1, 2, 3, ..., 3109 in the graph file, at least I can use this information to find out what is area #19's FIPS. If it is not reordered, I have no clue to find out the original FIPS of area #19.

The polygons are not sorted - so polygon 19 and relevant data should be accessible by subsetting the SPDF to row 19, e.g.:

map[19,]

I hope these answers are helpful,

James
